## Historical audit: S0235

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v2_1/results/smoke/fixed_h0/H0/smoke/commons_29022664/trajectory.jsonl`. References below are JSONL lines in this file; all observations shown are complete, so no split-observation offsets apply.

**Goal versus inference.** The task explicitly requested a separate-mesh reconstruction of a single indoor photograph, matching viewpoint, framing, placement and materials. The student's code interprets it as a kitchen; that interpretation and object names are not independent evidence of the unseen reference image (line 1, student `model_request`; line 3, student `model_response`).

| Stage | Observed evidence |
|---|---|
| Initial construction | The student supplied a nonempty program describing walls, floorboards, tiles, cabinets, two sink bowls, faucet and oven. It specified metal finishes, procedural stone and wood effects, a camera and lights. Handles were grouped as assets and sink openings used subtraction; actual contacts and alignment were not geometrically verified (line 3, student `model_response`; line 4, step 1 `execute`). |
| First validation and revision | Step 1 failed before rendering: the sink-rim fillet radius exceeded half its smallest dimension; `image` was null (line 5, `execution_result`). The error was actually sent to the student (line 6, student `model_request`). The next program reduced that radius from .026 to .006, enlarged the rim cutters, expanded the tile grid and shifted drawer handles; it was executed (lines 8–9, student `model_response` and step 2 `execute`). |
| Second validation | Step 2 advanced past the first error but failed at `world.use_nodes` because the scene world was `None`; again `image` was null (line 10, `execution_result`). The error and zero remaining executions were sent to the student (line 11, student `model_request`). |
| Final proposal | The final program creates a world if absent and replaces the solid cabinet body with panels, explicitly intending to avoid obstructing sink cavities. This is a proposed revision, not an observed execution or confirmed fix (line 13, student `model_response`). |

**Teacher and exploration.** No teacher detection, diagnosis, proposed update, receipt or adoption appears in this student trajectory. The input actually received between attempts was runner error feedback, not teacher advice. The student independently revised its program in response; the recorded sessions report no tool calls, and neither failed execution supplied a rendered image (lines 2, 5–7, 10–12). There is no evidence of visual iteration.

**Outcome and uncertainty.** This is a **technical build failure in both allowed executions**, not an empty patch; the final unexecuted program's outcome is unknown. No successful build or formal success is recorded. The reference and rendered images are not visible in this audit, so object count and identity in the photograph, part connection, pose, occlusion, camera match, lighting and texture fidelity cannot be verified. The second run reaching world setup does not establish a correct scene or render.

**Lessons.** Transferably, runtime feedback can isolate API constraints and expose later initialization failures, but passing one failure point is not visual validation. Here, the particular fillet and missing-world errors are task-specific observations; whether the final world initialization or hollow cabinet would yield a correct render remains an unresolved hypothesis.
